akhfash:4-4.t: [He said] ﴿إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾: an exception falling outside the first part of the speech.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ تُلْقُونَ﴾ conveying ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ the Prophet's ﷺ intention to raid them, which he had confided to you, while giving the impression it was Ḥunayn, ﴿بِالْمَوَدَّةِ﴾ between you and them. Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa wrote them a letter about that, because of the children and family, idolaters, he had among them; the Prophet ﷺ retrieved it from the one he had sent it with, through Allah the Exalted informing him of that, and he accepted Ḥāṭib's excuse in it. ﴿وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِمَا جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾, i.e. the religion of Islam and the Quran, ﴿يُخْرِجُونَ الرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ from Mecca by pressing hard on you, ﴿أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا﴾, i.e. because you believed, ﴿بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهَادًا﴾ for jihad ﴿فِي سَبِيلِي وَابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِي﴾ — and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition is indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then do not take them as allies" — ﴿تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِمَا أَخْفَيْتُمْ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُمْ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْهُ مِنْكُمْ﴾, i.e. the secret conveying of the Prophet's news to them, ﴿فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾: he has missed the path of guidance; and السَّوَاءُ originally means the middle.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿إِنْ يَثْقَفُوكُمْ﴾ gain the upper hand over you, ﴿يَكُونُوا لَكُمْ أَعْدَاءً وَيَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ with killing and beating ﴿وَأَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالسُّوءِ﴾ with abuse and insult; ﴿وَوَدُّوا﴾ they wished ﴿لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ أَرْحَامُكُمْ﴾ your kinship ﴿وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُمْ﴾, the idolaters for whose sake you confided the news, against the punishment in the Hereafter. ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ يُفْصَلُ﴾ — passive (built for the object) and active [يَفْصِلُ] — ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ and them; so you will be in Paradise and they among the whole of the disbelievers in the Fire. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ إِسْوَةٌ﴾, with kasra on the hamza and with ḍamma [أُسْوَةٌ], in both places: an example, ﴿حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾, i.e. in him, in word and deed, ﴿وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ﴾ of the believers, ﴿إِذْ قَالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إِنَّا بُرَآءُ﴾, plural of بَرِيءٌ, like ظَرِيفٌ, ﴿مِنْكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ﴾ we disown you, ﴿وَبَدَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَالْبَغْضَاءُ أَبَدًا﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed to wāw — ﴿حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ إِلَّا قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ﴾: excepted from أُسْوَةٍ, i.e. you are not to follow his example in that by seeking forgiveness for the disbelievers. And his saying ﴿وَمَا أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from His punishment and His reward, ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ — by it he alluded to the fact that he possesses nothing for him other than seeking forgiveness — is thus built upon it, excepted as regards what is meant by it, even though, as regards its outward sense, it is among the things in which he is to be followed: «قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا». And his seeking forgiveness for him was before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, as He mentioned in Barāʾa. ﴿رَبَّنَا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾: part of what was said by al-Khalīl (Abraham) and those with him, i.e. they said:

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, i.e. do not give them victory over us, so that they think they are upon the truth and are tempted, i.e. their minds are carried away on account of us; ﴿وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in Your dominion and Your making.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ﴾, O nation of Muhammad — the apodosis of an implied oath — ﴿فِيهِمْ إِسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِمَنْ كَانَ﴾: a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from كُمْ, with the preposition repeated [أُسْوَةٌ] [Translator's note: the bracketed variant reading of إِسْوَةٌ stands at this point in the source.] ﴿يَرْجُو اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ﴾, i.e. fears them, or expects the reward and the punishment. ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ﴾ by allying with the disbelievers, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ independent of His creation, ﴿الْحَمِيدُ﴾ to the people of obedience to Him.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ عَادَيْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ of the disbelievers of Mecca, in obedience to Allah the Exalted, ﴿مَوَدَّةً﴾ by guiding them to faith so that they become your allies. ﴿وَاللَّهُ قَدِيرٌ﴾ over that, and He did it after the conquest of Mecca; ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them for what is past, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿لَا يَنْهَاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ﴾ of the disbelievers ﴿فِي الدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ﴾: a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الَّذِينَ; ﴿وَتُقْسِطُوا﴾ judge ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ with qisṭ, i.e. with justice — and this was before the command to fight them. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ the just.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَنْهَاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ قَاتَلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ وَأَخْرَجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ وَظَاهَرُوا﴾ helped ﴿عَلَى إِخْرَاجِكُمْ أَنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾: a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الَّذِينَ, i.e. that you take them as allies. ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا جَاءَكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ﴾ by their tongues, ﴿مُهَاجِرَاتٍ﴾ from the disbelievers, after the truce with them at al-Ḥudaybiya on condition that whoever of them came to the believers would be returned, ﴿فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾ by an oath that they came out only out of desire for Islam, not from hatred of their disbelieving husbands nor from love for men among the Muslims; so he ﷺ used to make them swear. ﴿اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِهِنَّ فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ you think them, by the oath, ﴿مُؤْمِنَاتٍ فَلَا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ﴾ return them ﴿إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ لَا هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ وَآتُوهُمْ﴾, i.e. give their disbelieving husbands ﴿مَا أَنْفَقُوا﴾ on them of dowries. ﴿وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ with its condition ﴿إِذَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ their dowries. ﴿وَلَا تُمَسِّكُوا﴾, with tashdīd and without it [وَلَا تُمْسِكُوا], ﴿بِعِصَمِ الْكَوَافِرِ﴾: your wives, because their apostasy cuts off your marriage, with its condition; or those who join the idolaters as apostates, because your Islam cuts it off, with its condition. ﴿وَاسْأَلُوا﴾ demand ﴿مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ﴾ on them of dowries, in the case of apostasy, from those of the disbelievers who marry them, ﴿وَلْيَسْأَلُوا مَا أَنْفَقُوا﴾ on the emigrant women, as preceded: that they are to be given it. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ by it; ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَإِنْ فَاتَكُمْ شَيْءٌ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ﴾, i.e. one or more of them, or something of their dowries, through going ﴿إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ as apostates, ﴿فَعَاقَبْتُمْ﴾ and you raided and took spoils, ﴿فَآتُوا الَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتْ أَزْوَاجُهُمْ﴾ from the spoils ﴿مِثْلَ مَا أَنْفَقُوا﴾, because it was lost to them from the side of the disbelievers. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾. The believers did what they were commanded of giving to the disbelievers and to the believers; then this ruling was lifted.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا جَاءَكَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ يُبَايِعْنَكَ عَلَى أَنْ لَا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَسْرِقْنَ وَلَا يَزْنِينَ وَلَا يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ﴾, as used to be done in the Jāhiliyya of the burying of daughters, i.e. burying them alive, for fear of shame and poverty, ﴿وَلَا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتَانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾, i.e. a foundling child which they attribute to the husband; it is described with the description of a real child, for when the mother gives birth to it, it falls between her hands and her feet; ﴿وَلَا يَعْصِينَكَ فِي﴾ doing ﴿مَعْرُوفٍ﴾: it is what accords with obedience to Allah, such as abandoning wailing, tearing clothes, cutting the hair, rending the collar and scratching the face; ﴿فَبَايِعْهُنَّ﴾ — he ﷺ did that by word, and did not shake hands with any of them — ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُنَّ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: they are the Jews; ﴿قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e. of its reward, despite their certainty of it, because of their obstinacy against the Prophet despite their knowledge of his truthfulness, ﴿كَمَا يَئِسَ الْكُفَّارُ﴾ who are ﴿مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْقُبُورِ﴾, i.e. the buried, of the good of the Hereafter, since there are shown to them their seats in Paradise had they believed, and the Fire to which they are going.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional; ﴿فاتَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿شَيْءٌ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ both are attached to the verb as well, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَعاقَبْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَآتُوا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ذَهَبَتْ أَزْواجُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِثْلَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «الله»; ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to «مؤمنون»; ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), and the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the one addressed; ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿جاءَكَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْمُؤْمِناتُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿يُبايِعْنَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, the nūn being the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition; ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle that makes the verb accusative; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يُشْرِكْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the nūn being the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive governed by «على», and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿وَلا يَسْرِقْنَ، وَلا يَزْنِينَ، وَلا يَقْتُلْنَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿أَوْلادَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَلا يَأْتِينَ﴾ conjoined to «أن يشركن»; ﴿بِبُهْتانٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿يَفْتَرِينَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, the nūn being the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed (muḍāf) to «أيديهن», and ﴿أَرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾ is conjoined to «أيديهن». ﴿وَلا يَعْصِينَكَ﴾ conjoined to «أن لا يشركن»; ﴿فِي مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَبايِعْهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it and, like it, has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ «إنّ», its noun and its two predicates, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿لا تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿غَضِبَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوما». ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); ﴿يَئِسُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿كَما يَئِسَ الْكُفَّارُ﴾ «كما»: both are attached to [a word that is] the naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مِنْ أَصْحابِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْقُبُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, badal (substitute). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَدُوِّي﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾ conjoined to عدوي. ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿تُلْقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِالْمَوَدَّةِ﴾ both also attached to the verb.
﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿قَدْ كَفَرُوا﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يُخْرِجُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الرَّسُولَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ conjoined to الرسول; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكُمْ﴾ a badal from the Name of Majesty. ﴿أَنْ﴾ conditional. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿أَنْ﴾; the conditional particle in the Quranic text is ﴿إِنْ﴾.] ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun (ism). ﴿خَرَجْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the clause كنتم.. is initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿جِهاداً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿فِي سَبِيلِي﴾ both attached to جهادا. ﴿وَابْتِغاءَ﴾ conjoined to جهادا. ﴿مَرْضاتِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تُسِرُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿بِالْمَوَدَّةِ﴾ both also attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial. ﴿أَنَا أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to أعلم. ﴿أَخْفَيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَما أَعْلَنْتُمْ﴾ conjoined to ما أخفيتم. ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْهُ﴾ a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ, and an imperfect verb, jussive, and the hāʾ is its object, the fāʿil being latent. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification. ﴿ضَلَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿سَواءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to السبيل. ﴿السَّبِيلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the verbal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause من.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿إِنْ يَثْقَفُوكُمْ﴾ إن is conditional, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its noun (ism); the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿أَعْداءً﴾ the khabar of يكونوا. ﴿وَيَبْسُطُوا﴾ an imperfect verb conjoined to يكونوا. ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَلْسِنَتَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أيديهم. ﴿بِالسُّوءِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَوَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ لو is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from لو and what follows it is the object of ودوا.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن, and its object. ﴿أَرْحامُكُمْ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to أرحامكم. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَفْصِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) بصير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t:
﴿قَدْ كانَتْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq) and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان. ﴿أُسْوَةٌ﴾ its postponed noun (ism). ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of أسوة; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أسوة. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to إبراهيم. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from إبراهيم. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِقَوْمِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّا بُرَآؤُا﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to برآء.
﴿وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ both conjoined to منكم, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَفَرْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَبَدا بَيْنَنا﴾ a past verb and an adverb of place, and ﴿بَيْنَكُمُ﴾ is conjoined to بيننا. ﴿الْعَداوَةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَالْبَغْضاءُ﴾ conjoined to العداوة. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and genitive. ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after حتى. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَحْدَهُ﴾ ḥāl; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بدا. ﴿إِلَّا قَوْلَ﴾ a particle of exception and the excepted, accusative. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِأَبِيهِ﴾ both attached to قول. ﴿لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿أَمْلِكُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both also attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أملك. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ both attached to توكلنا; the vocative clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿تَوَكَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَإِلَيْكَ﴾ both attached to what follows them. ﴿أَنَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِلَيْكَ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿لا تَجْعَلْنا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and ﴿نا﴾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) فتنة; the vocative and verbal clauses are both resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَاغْفِرْ﴾ a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), and ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ two khabars (predicates); the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), and the verbal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كانَ لَكُمْ﴾ kāna, and a preposition and its genitive noun as its fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar. ﴿أُسْوَةٌ﴾ the postponed noun (ism) of كان. ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the clause is the response to the implied oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from لكم. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir). ﴿يَرْجُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the Name of Majesty is its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of كان, and the clause كان.. is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَالْيَوْمَ﴾ conjoined to الله. ﴿الْآخِرَ﴾ a ṣifa. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَتَوَلَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ﴾ two khabars; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the clause من.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ﴾ ʿasā and its noun (ism), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is the khabar (predicate) of عسى, and the clause عسى is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ conjoined to بينكم. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عادَيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَوَدَّةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَاللَّهُ قَدِيرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿لا يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَنِ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَمْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي الدِّينِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ﴾ conjoined to لم يقاتلوكم, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الذين. ﴿وَتُقْسِطُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿يُحِبُّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:9-9.t:
﴿إِنَّما يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and an imperfect verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿عَنِ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿قاتَلُوكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي الدِّينِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).
﴿أَخْرَجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ظاهَرُوا عَلى إِخْراجِكُمْ﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الذين. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَتَوَلَّهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause من..
is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جاءَكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and ﴿الْمُؤْمِناتُ﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مُهاجِراتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿بِإِيمانِهِنَّ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم; the nominal clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿إن﴾ conditional. ﴿عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُؤْمِناتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَلا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object. ﴿إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿هُنَّ حِلٌّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to حل; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحِلُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ both attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿آتُوهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its first object. ﴿ما﴾ its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿جُناحَ﴾ its noun (ism), indeclinable on fatḥa. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿إِذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of time, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ its second object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَلا تُمْسِكُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِعِصَمِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْكَوافِرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَسْئَلُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْفَقْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلْيَسْئَلُوا﴾ a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command (lām al-amr), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. And ﴿ذلِكُمْ حُكْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ with ḍamma; as muḍāf ilayhi the Quranic text has ﴿اللَّهِ﴾.] The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَحْكُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِياءَ تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ):
يا is a vocative particle; أيّها is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for alerting; الذين is a badal (substitute) of أيدي [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently a misprint for "أيّ"]; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); عدوي is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — it applies to one and more, because it is on the pattern of the maṣdar (verbal noun); عدوكم is conjoined to عدوي; and أولياء is the second mafʿūl bihi. The clause تلقون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تتخذوا; it may also be in the position of the accusative as an adjective of أولياء; or it may be explicative, with no grammatical position, [explaining] their taking them as allies. It has also been said that it is resumptive, brought to inform of that. تلقون is a verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, its implied form being "the news of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ"; it has also been said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) and المودّة is the mafʿūl bihi, with no omission. إليهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تلقون.
(وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِما جاءَكُمْ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is circumstantial; قد is a particle of realisation; كفروا is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl from لا تتخذوا or from تلقون, the meaning being: do not love them while this is their state. بما is attached to كفروا; the clause جاءكم is the ṣila; and من الحق is a ḥāl.
(يُخْرِجُونَ الرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكُمْ): the clause يخرجون is resumptive or explicative of their disbelief, so it has no grammatical position on either view; it may also be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of كفروا. الرسول is the object; إياكم is conjoined to الرسول; أن تؤمنوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. because of your believing in Allah; بالله is attached to تؤمنوا; and ربكم is a badal.
(إِنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهاداً فِي سَبِيلِي وَابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِي): إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun; the clause خرجتم is the predicate of كنتم; جهادا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. for the sake of jihad — and the accusative may also be as a ḥāl, i.e. in the state of your being strivers. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by His saying لا تتخذوا.
(تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِما أَخْفَيْتُمْ وَما أَعْلَنْتُمْ): the clause تسرون is either resumptive or subordinate to تلقون إليهم as a badal of part for whole, because conveying love is more general than [doing so] secretly and openly. تسرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the mafʿūl bihi is omitted; بالمودّة is attached to تسرون, or the bāʾ is redundant in the object, after the pattern of what preceded in تلقون إليهم بالمودّة. The wāw is circumstantial; أنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم the khabar (predicate), as an elative (ism tafḍīl); بما is attached to أعلم; the clause أخفيتم is the ṣila of ما. أعلم may also be an imperfect verb. وما أعلنتم is conjoined to بما أخفيتم.
(وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْهُ مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ): the wāw is conjunctive or resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يفعله is the protasis, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿ links the apodosis because it is joined with قد; ضلّ is a verb whose fāʿil is هو, and سواء السبيل is its object. It has also been said that ضلّ is intransitive, so سواء السبيل is accusative as an adverb of place.
(إِنْ يَثْقَفُوكُمْ يَكُونُوا لَكُمْ أَعْداءً): إن is conditional; يثقفوكم is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; يكونوا is the apodosis, the sign of its jussive also being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its noun and أعداء its predicate; and لكم is a ḥāl. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«ثقفت الشيء ثقفا, of the pattern of تعب: I took it; ثقفت الرجل في الحرب: I caught up with him; ثقفته: I got the better of him; ثقفت الحديث: I understood it quickly; the active participle is ثقيف.»
(وَيَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالسُّوءِ): conjoined to يكونوا; إليكم is attached to يبسطوا; أيديهم is the mafʿūl bihi; ألسنتهم is conjoined to أيديهم; and بالسوء is a ḥāl.
(وَوَدُّوا لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ): also conjoined, to the clause of condition and consequence; so He the Exalted has given two pieces of information: what the conditional clause contains, and their wishing that the believers disbelieve. The secret of the shift from the imperfect to the past will come. لو is maṣdar-forming; تكفرون is an imperfect verb, nominative; and لو with what lies in its scope is a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as the object of ودّوا.
(لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ أَرْحامُكُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to make known that their kin and children will not benefit them. لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; تنفعكم is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; the kāf is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and أرحامكم a postponed fāʿil; ولا أولادكم is conjoined to أرحامكم. يوم القيامة is an adverb attached to what precedes it, i.e. "they will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection", with a pause on it; or attached to what follows it, i.e. "He will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection". يفصل is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is هو, i.e. Allah the Exalted; and يُفصَل has been read in the passive. بينكم is an adverb attached to يفصل in any case.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): الله is a mubtadaʾ; بما is attached to بصير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila; and بصير is the khabar of الله.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وودّوا لو تكفرون» He shifted from the imperfect, which suits what precedes it, to the past, although the context requires it to be a future imperfect, by regarding it as having already happened; i.e. their wishing for your disbelief is what matters to them, and nothing equals it in weight. That is, they want to inflict on you all the harms of this world and of religion, and your reverting to disbelief is the foremost of the harms to you, because they know that religion is dearer to you than your lives. This is of the wonderful [modes of] expression.

* Benefits:
It is now time to convey to you a full summary of the story because of which the sura was revealed, for the enjoyment and benefit in it. The Imams have related — the wording being Muslim's — from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdād, and said: "Go to Rawḍat Khākh" — [read] as a triptote and as a diptote — a place twelve miles from Medina, "for there is a woman travelling in a litter there who has a letter; take it from her." So we set off, our horses racing (nuhādī), i.e. we made them go fast, and there we came upon a woman. We said, "Bring out the letter." She said, "I have no letter." We said, "You will bring out the letter, or you will cast off your clothes." So she brought it out from her braids, and we brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in it was: From Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa to some people among the idolaters of Mecca, informing them of something of the affair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Ḥāṭib, what is this?" He said: "Do not hasten against me, O Messenger of Allah. I was a man attached to Quraysh" — Sufyān said: he was their ally and not one of them — "and those emigrants who are with you have kinsmen by whom they protect their families. Since I lacked that kinship among them, I wanted to do them a favour by which they would protect my relatives. I did not do it out of disbelief, nor apostasy from my religion, nor contentment with disbelief after Islam. And I knew that Allah would send down His might upon them, that my letter would not avail them anything, and that Allah would grant you victory over them." The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has spoken the truth." ʿUmar said: "Let me, O Messenger of Allah, strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He witnessed Badr; and what do you know — perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء» (the verse). It has been said that the woman's name was Sāra, and she was a freedwoman of Abū ʿAmr ibn Ṣayfī ibn Hāshim.

The text of the letter:
As for the text of Ḥāṭib's letter, it is: «To proceed: the Messenger of Allah has set out towards you with an army like the night, moving like a torrent. I swear by Allah, if he marched against you alone, Allah would give him victory over you and fulfil His promise to him concerning you, for Allah is his Protector and Helper.»
Al-Qushayrī and al-Thaʿlabī mentioned that Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa was a man from the people of Yemen, and in Mecca he was an ally of the Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, the clan of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām; it has also been said he was an ally of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām. Sāra came from Mecca to Medina while the Messenger of Allah was preparing for the conquest of Mecca. The Messenger of Allah said to her: "Have you come as an emigrant, O Sāra?" She said: "No." He said: "Have you come as a Muslim?" She said: "No." He said: "Then what brought you?"
She said: "You were the family, the patrons, the root and the clan; some of the patrons have gone" — meaning they were killed on the day of Badr — "and I have fallen into severe need, so I have come to you that you may give to me and clothe me." He, upon him be blessing and peace, said: "And where are you with respect to the young men of Mecca?" — she was a singer. She said: "Nothing has been requested of me since the battle of Badr." So the Messenger of Allah urged the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to give to her, and they clothed her, gave her a mount and gave to her. She set out for Mecca, and Ḥāṭib came to her and said: "I will give you ten dinars and a cloak on condition that you deliver this letter to the people of Mecca." And he wrote in the letter: "The Messenger of Allah intends [to attack] you, so take your precautions" — to the end of the story.

dervis-irab:4-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُسْوَةٌ): with ḍamma and with kasra on the hamza, and it has been read with both; i.e. the model, and that by which one consoles oneself. The plural is أسى, also with ḍamma and kasra on the hamza.
(بَراءٌ): plural of بريء, like ظريف and ظرفاء; it also has the plural براء with kasra on the bāʾ, like ظريف and ظراف [Translator's note: the source prints "ظرف"]; and براء with ḍamma on the bāʾ, like تؤام and ظؤار; and أبراء and أبرياء. البريء is the pure, the free [of something], and the opposite of the guilty and the accused.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ كانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْراهِيمَ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ): a resumptive statement brought to strike the example worthy of imitation in the prohibition of befriending the disbelievers and inclining towards enemies, and [to show] that breasts folded upon rancour must remain in their enmity until the existing cause disappears; when it disappears, enmity turns to affection and hatred to love. قد is a particle of realisation; كانت is a defective past verb; لكم is its fronted predicate and أسوة its postponed noun; and حسنة is a naʿt (adjective) of أسوة. As for في إبراهيم:
you may attach it to an omitted [word] as a second adjective of أسوة, or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, since it has been qualified. The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «There are several views on it: first, it is another adjective of أسوة; second, it is attached to حسنة as an adverbial is attached to its governor; third, that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in حسنة; fourth, that it be the predicate of كان, and لكم is an explanation. It may not be attached to أسوة, because it has been qualified.» A number of parsers rejected the last point of Abū al-Baqāʾ, because with adverbials [and prepositional phrases] what is overlooked is not overlooked with others. الذين is conjoined to إبراهيم; and معه is an adverb of place attached to an omitted [word], which is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.
(إِذْ قالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إِنَّا بُرَآؤُا مِنْكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): إذ is an adverb of past time, i.e. "when they said", and it is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of إبراهيم والذين معه; this is the best of the strained parsings mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ and others. The clause قالوا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; لقومهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قالوا; إنّ and its noun, and برآء is its predicate, the clause being the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); منكم is attached to برآء; مما is conjoined to منكم; the clause تعبدون is the ṣila; and من دون الله is a ḥāl.
(كَفَرْنا بِكُمْ وَبَدا بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمُ الْعَداوَةُ وَالْبَغْضاءُ أَبَداً حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ): the clause explains the disowning of them and of what they worship; you may also make it a ḥāl, i.e. we have disowned you, being disbelievers in you. كفرنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بكم is attached to كفرنا; بدا is a past verb; بيننا is an adverb attached to بدا; بينكم is an adverb conjoined to بيننا; العداوة is the fāʿil; البغضاء is conjoined to العداوة; أبدا is an adverb also attached to بدا; حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; تؤمنوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; بالله is attached to تؤمنوا; and وحده is a ḥāl.
(إِلَّا قَوْلَ إِبْراهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَما أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): إلا is a particle of exception; قول إبراهيم is excepted from أسوة حسنة, because the saying is part of the model; so it is a connected exception, as if it were said: you have in him a good model in all his states of word and deed, except his saying such-and-such. It has also been said that it is a disconnected exception, the meaning being: but Ibrāhīm's saying to his father "I will surely ask forgiveness for you" — do not imitate him in it. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: It appears that it is part of the completion of Ibrāhīm's saying, connected with what precedes the exception, and it is among the things in which he is to be imitated; the exception separates them out of concern for the exception and because of its closeness to what is excepted from. لأبيه is attached to قول. لأستغفرنّ: the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); أستغفرن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا"; the clause is the object of the saying; and لك is attached to أستغفرنّ. The wāw is circumstantial or conjunctive, since the clause is part of the completion of Ibrāhīm's saying; so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أستغفرنّ, i.e. "I will ask forgiveness for you, and nothing is within my power but asking forgiveness"; so it is built on what precedes it and arranged after it by way of being a ḥāl; and conjunction is also permissible. ما is negating; أملك is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنا"; لك is attached to أملك; من الله is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of شيء; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and شيء is genitive in form and accusative in position as the object of أملك.
(رَبَّنا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ): the completion of what was said by al-Khalīl Ibrāhīm and those with him; so it belongs to what is excepted from, and he is to be imitated in it. So in meaning it comes before the exception, and the exception clause is parenthetical in the midst of what is excepted from. The wording of al-Kashshāf: «If you say: with what is His saying ربنا عليك توكلنا connected? I say: with what precedes the exception, and it is part of the good model. It may also mean: "Say: Our Lord", as a command from Allah the Exalted to the believers to say it, and a teaching from Him to them, completing what He enjoined on them of cutting the ties between them and the disbelievers, and of following the example of Ibrāhīm and his people in disowning them; and drawing attention to turning to Allah and seeking refuge in Him from the trial of the people of disbelief, and seeking forgiveness for what they had neglected.» I.e. it is then the object of an omitted saying. ربنا is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; عليك is attached to توكلنا; إليك is attached to أنبنا; the wāw is conjunctive; إليك is a fronted khabar (predicate) and المصير a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
(رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَاغْفِرْ لَنا رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): ربنا is also the one addressed, a muḍāf; لا is prohibitive, intended as supplication; تجعلنا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; نا is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and فتنة the second mafʿūl bihi. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the agent, i.e. do not make us a cause of trial to them by their gaining victory over us, so that their minds are shaken and they are tempted, and their souls entice them [to think] that they are in the right; or in the sense of the patient, as al-Bayḍāwī set out, i.e. do not make us
tried by them by giving them power over us, so that they try us with a punishment we have no strength to bear. للذين is attached to فتنة on both views; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of the relative noun; ربنا is the one addressed, a muḍāf, repeated for emphasis; إنّ and its noun; أنت is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; العزيز is the khabar of إنّ, or the khabar of أنت, the clause then being the khabar of إنّ; and الحكيم is a second khabar in either case.
(لَقَدْ كانَ لَكُمْ فِيهِمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ): the clause follows the clause قد كانت لكم أسوة as an emphasis of it, brought for intensity in urging the ruling. The lām prepares for an implied oath; قد is a particle of realisation; كان is a defective past verb; لكم is its fronted predicate; فيهم is a ḥāl; أسوة is the postponed noun of كان and حسنة an adjective of أسوة; لمن is a badal of part for whole of لكم, with repetition of the preposition — it has also been said to be a badal of inclusion; the clause كان is the ṣila of من; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "هو"; the clause يرجو الله is the predicate of كان; and اليوم الآخر is conjoined to الله.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يتول is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿ links the apodosis, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then the evil consequence of his turning away is upon himself"; and إنّ with its noun and its two predicates is the reason for the apodosis.
(عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ عادَيْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَوَدَّةً): عسى is one of the verbs of hope; الله is its noun; أن يجعل is in the place of the predicate; بينكم is an adverb in the place of the second object of يجعل; بين الذين عاديتهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has عاديتم] is conjoined to the adverb; مودّة is the first object of يجعل; and منهم is a ḥāl from الذين عاديتم.
(وَاللَّهُ قَدِيرٌ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, with their like conjoined to them.

dervis-irab:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(لا يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the permission to maintain ties with those who did not fight the believers and did not expel them from their homes. لا is negating; ينهاكم الله is an imperfect verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); عن الذين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينهاكم; the clause لم يقاتلوكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and في الدين is attached to يقاتلوكم, i.e. on account of it.
(وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوا إِلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ): ولم يخرجوكم is conjoined to لم يقاتلوكم; من دياركم is attached to يخرجوكم; أن تبرّوهم is in the position of the genitive as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of الذين; وتقسطوا إليهم is conjoined to تبروهم; and إنّ with its noun, the clause يحبّ المقسطين being its predicate. Beautiful is al-Zamakhsharī's saying in this connection: «And it suffices you that Allah's enjoining the believers to deal justly with those who associate partners with Him and to avoid wronging them speaks eloquently of the state of a Muslim who dares to wrong his Muslim brother.»
(إِنَّما يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ قاتَلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ): إنما is [إنّ] restrained [from governing] by the restraining [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ينهاكم الله is an imperfect verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; عن الذين is attached to ينهاكم; the clause قاتلوكم is the ṣila of الذين; and في الدين is attached to قاتلوكم.
(وَأَخْرَجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ وَظاهَرُوا عَلى إِخْراجِكُمْ أَنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ): أخرجوكم is conjoined to قاتلوكم; من دياركم is attached to أخرجوكم; ظاهروا is also conjoined; على إخراجكم is attached to ظاهروا, i.e. they helped in expelling you; and أن with what lies in its scope is a badal of inclusion of الذين. Its counterpart has preceded.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يتولهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʿ is linking; the clause أولئك هم الظالمون is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من.

dervis-irab:10-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ): then test them and try them. That is why the sura was named al-Mumtaḥina, with kasra on the ḥāʾ, i.e. the one that tests — meaning the woman or the group that tests, since in it the group of believers is commanded to test. If the ḥāʾ is given fatḥa, the meaning is "the sura of the emigrant woman" concerning whom the verse of testing was revealed; her story will come in the section on benefits.
(بِعِصَمِ الْكَوافِرِ): العصم is the plural of عصمة, which here is the marriage contract; everything by which a thing is held fast is عصام and عصمة. The properties of [roots with] ʿayn and ṣād as first and second radicals have passed. الكوافر is the plural of كافرة, like ضوارب from ضاربة. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «Al-Karkhī said: الكوافر includes men and women. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said to him: The grammarians hold this only for women, as the plural of كافرة. He said: Is it not said طائفة كافرة (a disbelieving faction) and فرقة كافرة (a disbelieving sect)? Abū ʿAlī said: I was dumbfounded, and I said: This is a confirmation.» This al-Karkhī was a Muʿtazilite jurist, and Abū ʿAlī was also a Muʿtazilite, so this derivation pleased him; but it amounts to nothing, because كافرة is not said in describing men except as following its qualified noun, or with that noun omitted but intended; otherwise, فاعلة is not pluralised as فواعل except when it is for the feminine.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا جاءَكُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتُ مُهاجِراتٍ فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ): إذا is an adverb of future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the clause جاءكم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; المؤمنات is a postponed fāʿil (agent); مهاجرات is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʿ is linking; and the clause امتحنوهنّ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; it is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمانِهِنَّ فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِناتٍ فَلا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ): الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم the khabar (predicate); بإيمانهنّ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم, because it is an elative (afʿal tafḍīl). The fāʿ is conjunctive; إن is conditional; علمتموهنّ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) — a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi — and مؤمنات is the second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a request clause; لا is prohibitive; ترجعوهنّ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; and إلى الكفّار is attached to ترجعوهنّ.
(لا هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَهُمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ): the clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for His saying فلا ترجعوهنّ. لا is negating; هنّ is a mubtadaʾ and حلّ the khabar; لهم is attached to حلّ; and ولا هم يحلّون لهنّ is conjoined to the preceding clause, parallel to it.
(وَآتُوهُمْ ما أَنْفَقُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; آتوهم is a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; it is an imperative], its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, the pronoun referring to the disbelievers, i.e. give their disbelieving husbands what they spent on them. ما is the second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause أنفقوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, i.e. what they spent on them of dowries.
(وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ إِذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is the lā of generic negation; جناح is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; عليكم is the predicate of لا; أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; تنكحوهنّ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "in your marrying them", the preposition and its noun being attached to جناح. إذا is an adverb containing the meaning of condition; the clause آتيتموهنّ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; and أجورهنّ is the second object of آتيتموهنّ.
(وَلا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الْكَوافِرِ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تمسكوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and بعصم الكوافر is attached to تمسكوا.
(وَسْئَلُوا ما أَنْفَقْتُمْ وَلْيَسْئَلُوا ما أَنْفَقُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; اسألوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil and ما is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause أنفقتم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما. وليسألوا: the wāw is conjunctive, the lām is the lām of command, يسألوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, ما is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause أنفقوا is the ṣila.
(ذلِكُمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the ruling contained in the verses, and حكم الله is the khabar; the clause يحكم is resumptive or a ḥāl from حكم الله; بينكم is an adverb attached to يحكم; الله is a mubtadaʾ, عليم a first khabar and حكيم a second khabar.
(وَإِنْ فاتَكُمْ شَيْءٌ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ فَعاقَبْتُمْ فَآتُوا الَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتْ أَزْواجُهُمْ مِثْلَ ما أَنْفَقُوا): the wāw is conjunctive, so that the rulings follow in sequence. إن is conditional; فاتكم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; شيء is the fāʿil of فاتكم. In من أزواجكم there are two views. The first: it may be attached to فاتكم, i.e. on the part of your wives, and by "something" is meant the dowry the husband paid, since it has come down that when a Muslim man's wife fled to the disbelievers, Allah commanded the believers to give him what he had paid. The second view: it is attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of شيء; then شيء may mean what preceded of dowries, but on this view a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "of the dowries of your wives", so that the qualified noun and its adjective correspond; or شيء may mean the women, i.e. a kind and category of them. إلى الكفار is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. going or preceding. فعاقبتم: the fāʿ is conjunctive and عاقبتم is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. then you raided, took booty and struck them in fighting. فآتوا: the fāʿ is linking; آتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause ذهبت أزواجهم is the ṣila; مثل is the second mafʿūl bihi; ما is a relative noun to which مثل is annexed; and the clause أنفقوا is the ṣila.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ): اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; به is attached to مؤمنون; مؤمنون is the khabar of أنتم; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of الذي.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا جاءَكَ الْمُؤْمِناتُ يُبايِعْنَكَ عَلى أَنْ لا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئاً): إذا is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition; the clause جاءك is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and المؤمنات the fāʿil; يبايعنك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because of its connection with the nūn of the feminine plural; the nūn is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is circumstantial, i.e. in the state of their seeking to pledge allegiance. على is a preposition, and أن with what lies in its scope is in the position of the genitive by على, the preposition and its noun being attached to يبايعنك; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. anything of associating partners.
(وَلا يَسْرِقْنَ وَلا يَزْنِينَ وَلا يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلادَهُنَّ وَلا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ وَلا يَعْصِينَكَ فِي مَعْرُوفٍ فَبايِعْهُنَّ): speech conjoined to أن لا يشركن. The meaning of يقتلن أولادهنّ is as was the case in the time of the Jāhiliyya, of burying daughters alive. ببهتان is attached to يأتين; the clause يفترينه is circumstantial; بين أيديهنّ وأرجلهنّ: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in يفترينه, i.e. they bring a foundling child and attribute it to the husband. Beautiful is its being described with the attribute of a real child, for when a mother gives birth to a child it falls between her hands and her feet. فبايعهنّ: the fāʿ links the answer of إذا, and the clause بايعهنّ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُنَّ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; استغفر is an imperative verb; لهنّ is attached to استغفر; الله is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause إن الله غفور رحيم is the reason for the command to seek forgiveness.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْماً غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to close the sura with the like of what it opened with: the prohibition of taking the disbelievers as allies. لا is prohibitive; تتولوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; قوما is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause غضب الله عليهم is an adjective of قوما.
(قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ كَما يَئِسَ الْكُفَّارُ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْقُبُورِ): the clause is a second adjective of قوما, or a ḥāl after it has been qualified. قد is a particle of realisation; يئسوا is a verb and its fāʿil; من الآخرة is attached to يئسوا; كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); يئس الكفار is a verb and its fāʿil, the clause having no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative. In من أصحاب القبور there are two views. One: من is for the beginning of the extent, like the first [من], and the meaning is that they do not at all believe with certainty in the resurrection of the dead, so their despair of the Hereafter is like their despair of their dead, because they believe they will not be raised. The second: من is for explaining the genus, meaning that the disbelievers are the people of the graves; so the preposition and its noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, and what the second يئس is attached to is omitted, the meaning being: these have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers, being among the people of the graves, have despaired of the good of the Hereafter.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفّار من أصحاب القبور» there is the device of istiṭrād (digression), a lofty device among the devices of bayān. Al-Ḥātimī mentioned that he took this name from the poet al-Buḥturī, and Ibn al-Muʿtazz called it "going out from one meaning to another". Of it in the Glorious Quran is «ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود», for here He digressed. In the verse we are dealing with, He censured the Jews and digressed from censuring them to censuring the idolaters, with a fine kind of relation. Istiṭrād linguistically is the maṣdar of استطرد الفارس من قرنه في الحرب (the horseman feigned flight from his opponent in war), that is, he flees from before him, making him imagine defeat, then wheels round on him while he is off guard. Technically, it is that you are on one of the themes of poetry, making it seem that you are continuing in it, then you go out from it to another because of a relation between them; the name of the one digressed to must be stated explicitly, on condition that he has not been mentioned before; then you return to the first, or it is the end of the speech. It has been said that the first instance of this kind that has come down and become proverbial is the saying of al-Samawʾal:
وإنّا لقوم لا نرى القتل سبة ... إذا ما رأته عامر وسلول
(We are a people who do not consider being killed a disgrace, whereas ʿĀmir and Salūl consider it so.)
See how he went out, while engaged in boasting, into satire, and how finely he returned to what he had been on of boasting by his saying:
يقرب حب الموت آجالنا لنا ... وتكرهه آجالهم فتطول
(Love of death brings our appointed terms near to us, while their terms hate it and so grow long.)
And of it is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
إن كنت كاذبة الذي حدّثتني ... فنجوت منجى الحارث بن هشام
ترك الأحبة أن يقاتل دونهم ... ونجا برأس طمرة ولجام
(If you have lied in what you told me, then may you escape as al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām escaped: he left his loved ones rather than fight for them, and escaped on the head of a swift mare with a bridle.)
See how he went out from love poetry to satirising al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, the brother of Abū Jahl, who embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest, became a good Muslim, and died on the day of al-Yarmūk in Syria. Also of it is the saying of al-Buḥturī, from an ode describing a horse:
كالهيكل المبني إلا أنه ... في الحسن جاء كصورة في هيكل
ملك العيون فإن بدا أعطيته ... نظر المحب إلى الحبيب المقبل
ما إن يعاف قذى ولو أوردته ... يوما خلائق حمدويه الأحول
(Like a built temple, except that in beauty it came like an image in a temple; it masters the eyes, and when it appears you give it the look of a lover at the approaching beloved; it does not shun dirty water, even if one day you led it to water at the character of squint-eyed Ḥamdawayh.)
And like it is the saying of someone describing wine that was cooked until it became clear and pure:
لم يبق منها وقود الطابخين لها ... إلا كما أبقت الأنواء من داري
(The fire of those who cooked it left of it only as much as the rain-storms have left of my house.)
How sweet is his digression from describing the wine to describing his house as ruined!
Among the rarities of this chapter is digression from satire to satire, as in the saying of Jarīr satirising al-Farazdaq:
لها برص بأسفل أسكيتها ... كعنفقة الفرزدق حين شابا
(She has leprous patches on the lower sides of her private parts, like al-Farazdaq's chin-tuft when it turned grey.)

* Benefits:
This sura contains historical and legislative benefits; we cite those of them related to the subject of our book, and refer the reader to the books of jurisprudence and the lengthy commentaries:
1- History relates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished receiving the pledge of the men on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, he began receiving the pledge of the women while he was on al-Ṣafā, with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb below him taking their pledge at his command and conveying to them from him. Hind bint ʿUtba, the wife of Abū Sufyān, was veiled and disguised among the women, fearing that the Messenger of Allah would recognise her because of what she had done to Ḥamza on the day of Uḥud. She said: "By Allah, you are taking from us an undertaking that I did not see you take from the men" — that day he had taken the pledge of the men on Islam and jihad only. The Messenger of Allah said: "And that they will not steal." She said: "Abū Sufyān is stingy, and I have taken small amounts of his wealth; I do not know whether they are lawful for me or not." Abū Sufyān said: "Whatever you took in what is past and what remains is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and recognised her, and said to her: "And you are indeed Hind bint ʿUtba?" She said: "Yes, so pardon what is past, O Prophet of Allah, may Allah pardon you." He said: "And that they will not commit fornication." She said: "Does a free woman commit fornication?"
In one narration: "No woman among them has ever committed fornication." He, upon him be blessing and peace, said: "And that they will not kill their children." She said: "We raised them when small and you killed them when grown; you and they know best" — her son Ḥanẓala ibn Abī Sufyān had been killed on the day of Badr. ʿUmar laughed until he fell on his back, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. He said: "And that they will not bring a slander." She said: "By Allah, slander is an ugly thing, and you command us only to right guidance and noble character." He said: "And that they will not disobey you in what is right." She said: "By Allah, we have not sat in this sitting of ours with any thought in ourselves of disobeying you in anything."
2- Various narrations have been mentioned about the manner of burying daughters alive; we consider the closest of them to reason what has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «In the Jāhiliyya, when a woman's delivery drew near, she would dig a pit and go into labour at the edge of the pit; if she gave birth to a girl she threw her into the pit and put the earth back over her, and if she gave birth to a boy she kept him. And in the Jāhiliyya, when a daughter was born to a man and he wanted to let her live, he would clothe her in a garment of wool or hair, and she would herd camels and sheep for him in the desert; and if he wanted to kill her, he would leave her until, when she was "sudāsiyya", i.e. six years old, he would say to her mother: Perfume her and adorn her, so that I may take her to her in-laws. He would have dug a well for her in the desert, and he would take her to the well and say to her: Look into it; then he would push her from behind and heap the earth upon her.
[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of Ibn ʿAbbās's report is missing in the source.]

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذَا جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتُ مُهَاجِرَاتٍ فَٱمْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾.
It means: make them swear an oath. That is because when the Prophet ﷺ made peace with the people of Mecca at al-Ḥudaybiya, and the document had been sealed, Subayʿa bint al-Ḥārith al-Aslamiyya came out to him as a Muslim. Her husband came and said: Return her to me, for that is in the condition we have against you, and this is the clay of the writing, not yet dry. So this verse came down: ﴿فَلاَ تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ لاَ هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَّهُمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ﴾.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made her swear: that nothing brought you out to us except eagerness for Islam and desire for it, and that no misdeed you committed brought you out, nor hatred of your husband. She swore, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her husband her dowry, and the revelation came down: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُواْ بِعِصَمِ ٱلْكَوَافِرِ﴾.
Whoever had a wife in Mecca who refused to become Muslim, the marriage bond (ʿiṣma) between her and her husband was cut; and whichever of their women came out to the Muslims as a Muslim, her bond with her unbelieving husband was cut, and the Muslims may marry her without a waiting period (ʿidda).
His saying: ﴿وَاسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ وَلْيَسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقُواْ﴾.
He is saying: ask the people of Mecca to return to you the dowries of the women who go out from you to them as apostates, and let them ask for the dowries of those of their women who come out to you.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُواْ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it without doubling [تُمْسِكوا], and al-Ḥasan read it: تُمسّكوا; the meaning is close.
The Arabs say: أمسكت بك, مسكت بك and تمسّكت بك (I held fast to you).

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن فَاتَكُمْ شَيْءٌ﴾: [i.e.] escaped you. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وإن فاتكم أحد من أزواجكم". أحد is valid in the place of شىء, and شىء is valid in the place of أحد when it refers to people; but when شىء refers to something other than people, أحد is not valid in its place.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن فَاتَكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: [if one] escapes you — if a woman goes off and joins the people of Mecca as an unbeliever, and there is no covenant between you and them — and then you ﴿فَعَاقَبْتُمْ﴾, he is saying: you took booty, then give her husband her dowry from the booty before the fifth (khums) [is taken].
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, that he read "فعاقبتم" and explained it as: you took booty. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it: فعقّبتم, with doubling; it is like your saying تصعّر and تصاعر, among words of which I have informed you concerning the kinship of [the patterns] faʿʿaltu and fāʿaltu.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلاَدَهُنَّ﴾.
Al-Sulamī alone read it: ولا يقتّلن أولادهن. It is mentioned that when the Prophet ﷺ conquered Mecca he sat on al-Ṣafā with ʿUmar beside him, and the women came to him to give their pledge; among them was the daughter of ʿUtba [i.e. Hind]. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿لاَّ يُشْرِكْنَ بِٱللَّهِ شَيْئاً﴾ — he was saying: do not worship idols, do not steal and do not commit fornication — Hind said: And does a free woman commit fornication? He said: ʿUmar laughed, then said: No, by my life, a free woman does not commit fornication. He said: And when he said: Do not kill your children — this concerned the burying alive that the people of the Jāhiliyya used to practise, and they pledged not to do it — Hind said: We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتَٰنٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾.
A woman would pick up a foundling and say to her husband: This is my child by you. That is the fabricated slander (buhtān) [198/a].

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَتَوَلَّوْاْ قوْماً غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ قَدْ يَئِسُواْ مِنَ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
He is saying: [they have despaired] of the bliss of the Hereafter and its reward, just as the unbelievers have despaired of the people of the graves. He is saying: they [the dead unbelievers] know that there is no bliss for them in this world, since they have died and entered the graves.
And it is also said: just as the unbelievers who are among the people of the graves have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter and its bliss.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it: يُفصِّل بينكم; he [al-Farrāʾ] said: and Abū Zakariyyā [i.e. al-Farrāʾ himself] reads it the same way. ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read it: يَفْصل, and the people of Medina read it: يُفْصَل.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ﴾. He means Ḥāṭib; "فيهم" means: in Abraham. He is saying: in what Abraham and those with him did when they declared themselves free of their people. He is saying: Why did you not take Abraham as your example, O Ḥāṭib, and declare yourself free of your family as Abraham declared himself free? Then He said: ﴿إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لأَبِيهِ﴾, that is: you had an example in their deeds except in Abraham's saying "I will surely ask forgiveness [for you]", for in that you have no example.
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا بُرَءآؤاْ مِّنْكُمْ﴾. If you drop the hamza of برآء, you point to it with your chest and say: بُرَاء. Al-Farrāʾ said: [it is] a lengthening and a pointing toward the hamza, and it can only be captured precisely by hearing, [and he did not make it fully declinable (lam yujrihā)]. Some of the Arabs say: إِنا بِراءٌ منكم, making it fully declinable (yujrī); had it been read that way it would be a valid reading.
His saying: ﴿رَّبَّنَا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنَا﴾. That is: so say this saying yourselves; and it is also said that it is part of what Abraham, peace be upon him, and his people said.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا لاَ تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً﴾. [Meaning:] Do not let the unbelievers prevail over us, so that they would think that they are in the right and that we are in falsehood.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيْتُم مِّنْهُم مَّوَدَّةً﴾.
He is saying: perhaps the enmity between you will turn back into affection. Then the Prophet ﷺ married Umm Ḥabība, daughter of Abū Sufyān, and the marriage tie became affection.

farraa:8-9.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَنْهَاكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
These are Khuzāʿa: they had made a pact with the Prophet ﷺ that they would not [197/b] fight him and would not drive him out, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered that they be treated kindly and that the pact with them be kept until the end of its term. Then He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَنْهَاكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَاتَلُوكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخْرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَارِكُمْ وَظَاهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ إِخْرَاجِكُمْ أَن تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾: [that is,] that you support them; meaning the rest of the people of Mecca.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِٱلْمَوَدَّةِ﴾.
The entry of the bāʾ in «المودة» and its omission are the same. This is like your saying: «أظن أنك قائم» and «أظن بأنك قائم» (I think that you are standing), and «أريد بأن تذهب», «أريد بأن تقوم» (I want you to go / to stand). Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has said: ﴿ومَنْ يُرِدْ فيه بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾, inserting the bāʾ, while the meaning is: «ومن يرد فيه إلحادا» (whoever intends deviation in it).
Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
فلمّا رجتْ بالشُّرب هزَّلها العصا * شحيحٌ لهُ عند الإزاءِ نهيمُ
(When she hoped to drink, a niggardly man shook the stick at her, growling at the trough's mouth.)
Its meaning is: when she hoped that she would drink.
This sura was revealed about Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to attack the people of Mecca, a woman from the clients of Banū al-Muṭṭalib came to him, and the Muslims gave her gifts. When she wanted to return, Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa came to her and said: "I will give you ten dinars and clothe you with a cloak, on condition that you deliver a letter to the people of Mecca." So he wrote (a letter) with her, and she set off making for Mecca. Gabriel came down to the Prophet ﷺ (lit. may Allah bless them both) with the news, and he sent ʿAlī and al-Zubayr after her, saying: "If she hands the letter over to you, (well); [otherwise strike] [197/ا] her neck." They caught up with her, and she said: "Stand away from me, for I know that you will not believe me until you search me." He said: she took the letter and put it between two of her braids. They searched her and saw nothing, and turned back. Then ʿAlī said to al-Zubayr: "What have we done? The Messenger of Allah tells us that she has a letter, and we believe her?" So they turned back on her and said: "You will bring out your letter, or we will strike your neck." When she saw they were in earnest, she brought out the letter.
In it was: "From Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa to the people of Mecca. To proceed: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intends to attack you, so take your precautions," along with other things he wrote. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Ḥāṭib, and he admitted it to him and said: "What led me to this is that my family is in Mecca, and there is not [one] of your companions who does not have someone in Mecca to defend his family; so I wanted to gain favour with them so that they would look after my dependants.
