The clause «يسألوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا ترجعوهنّ.
The clause «أنفقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative noun (ما).
The clause «ذلك حكم اللَّه» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحكم ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the linking pronoun implied, i.e. "He judges between you by it".].
The clause «اللَّه عليم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
11- (الواو) a conjunction. (إن فاتكم) like إن علمتموهنّ. (من أزواجكم) attached to (فاتكم), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "on the side of your wives" [Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of شيء, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "something of the dowers of your wives".]. (إلى الكفّار) attached to a ḥāl from أزواجكم, i.e. "apostatising". (الفاء) a conjunction, and the second is connecting the apodosis. (مثل) second mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being آتوا. (ما) a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the returning pronoun being omitted. (الواو) a conjunction. (الذي) a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of the Name of Majesty. (به) attached to the khabar (مؤمنون).
The clause «فاتكم شيء ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause علمتموهنّ..
And what is between the two clauses is parenthetical.
The clause «عاقبتم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause فاتكم.
The clause «آتوا ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ذهبت أزواجهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أنفقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). The clause «اتّقوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «أنتم به مؤمنون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(10) عصم: plural of عصمة, a noun meaning the marriage bond; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn, and the pattern of عصم is فعل, with kasra then fatḥa.
(الكوافر) plural of كافرة, feminine of كافر, an active participle of the triliteral كفر; its pattern is فاعل, and الكوافر is فواعل.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {في إِبْرَاهِيمَ}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أُسوة»; you say, "I have an example (usra) in so-and-so." Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade its being attached to it, saying, "because it has already been qualified by an adjective." This is not to be minded, because in the case of an adverbial (ẓarf) what is tolerated is not tolerated in other things. The second is that it is attached to «حسنة», as an adverbial is attached to its governor. The third is that it is a second naʿt (adjective) of «أُسْوَة». The fourth is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «حسنةٌ». The fifth is that it is the khabar of kāna, with «لكم» as a clarification. The two readings of «أسْوة» and the discussion of its root have already been given in [Sūrat] al-Aḥzāb.
His saying: {إِذْ قَالُواْ}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is the khabar of kāna. The second is that it is attached to its khabar; Abū l-Baqāʾ stated both. Whoever allows kāna to govern an adverbial attaches it to kāna.
His saying: {بُرَآءُ}: this is the reading of the majority, with ḍamma on the bāʾ, fatḥa on the rāʾ and an alif between two hamzas, a plural of بريء, like كُرَماء as a plural of كريم. ʿĪsā al-Hamdhānī read it with kasra on the bāʾ and a single hamza after an alif, like كرام as a plural of كريم. ʿĪsā also, and Abū Jaʿfar, read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ and a hamza after an alif. There are several possibilities concerning it. The first is that it is likewise a plural of بَرِيْء, the original having a kasra on the bāʾ, and that a ḍamma was substituted for the kasra, like رُخال and رُباب; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second is that it is likewise a plural of بَرِيء, its original being برَآء as in the well-known reading, except that the first hamza was dropped for lightness; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. The third is that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for بريء, like تُؤَام and ظُؤَار, two collective nouns for تَوْءَم and ظِئْر. ʿĪsā also read «بَراء» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a hamza after an alif, like the one in [Sūrat] al-Zukhruf; and that is sound because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and a maṣdar applies to the plural just as it applies to the singular. Al-Zamakhsharī said, "البَراء and البراءة are like الظَّماء and الظَّماءة." Makkī said, "Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar permitted «بِراء» with kasra on the bāʾ, making it like كريم and كِرام. And al-Farrāʾ permitted «بَراء» with fatḥa on the bāʾ," and then he said, "and بَراء is originally a maṣdar," as if he had not come across it as a transmitted reading.
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from his saying «في إبراهيم», but a muḍāf must necessarily be omitted for the sentence to be sound, its implied form being: "in the sayings of Ibrāhīm, except his saying such-and-such." The second is that it is excepted from «أسوةٌ حسنةٌ», and that is permissible because the saying too belongs to the whole of the example, since an example (usra) is following a person in his words and deeds; so it is as if it were said: "You have in him an example in all his states, in word and deed, except his saying such-and-such." In my view this is clear; it requires no implied muḍāf and does not take the exception out of connectedness, which is its basic form, to disconnectedness. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only this. He said: "If you ask, from what is {إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} excepted? I say: from his saying «أُسْوَةٌ حسنةٌ», because by 'a good example' he meant their saying which it was incumbent upon them to follow and to take as a practice (sunna) to be followed.
If you ask: if his saying «لأستغفرَنَّ لك» is excepted from the saying that is a good example, then what of his saying {وَمَآ أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ الله مِن شَيْءٍ}, which does not deserve to be excepted? Do you not see his saying {قُلْ فَمَن يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ مِّنَ الله شَيْئاً} [al-Fatḥ: 11]? I say: he meant the exception of the whole of his statement to his father, the intent being the promise of asking forgiveness for him, and what comes after it is built upon it and follows it. It is as if he said: I will ask forgiveness for you, and nothing is within my power except asking forgiveness." The third: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, "It is possible that the exception is from the disavowal and severance that were mentioned, that is: you left no tie remaining except such-and-such." The fourth is that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), that is: "but the saying of Ibrāhīm." This is built, on the part of those who say it, on the view that the saying was not included under his words «أُسْوة»; and that is not accepted.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {رَبَّنَا}: it is possible that it is part of the speech of Ibrāhīm and those with him, and so belongs to the good example, the exception having separated the two. It is also possible that it is disconnected from what precedes, with an implied "say", being a teaching from Allah the Exalted to His servants, as if He had said to them: "Say: Our Lord, in You we have put our trust." The first is the clearer.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو}: a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in «لكم», a part substituted for the whole (badal baʿḍ min kull). The like of it has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Aḥzāb. The pronoun in «فيهم» refers to Ibrāhīm and those with him, and "the example" is repeated for emphasis.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {أَن تَبَرُّوهُمْ} and {أَن تَوَلَّوْهُمْ}: two badals (substitutes) from the «الذين» preceding them, badal ishtimāl (inclusion substitute). The meaning: Allah the Exalted does not forbid you to be dutiful to these; He only forbids you to take these as allies.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ}: it was said that it is an emphasis of the first, because the two are inseparable. It was also said that he meant the continuation of the ruling between them in the future, as it is at present, for as long as they are polytheists and the women are believers. His saying «المؤمنات» is naming a thing by what is close to it and approaches it, or by outward appearance. «مُهاجراتٌ» was also read with nominative ending, and it was explained as a badal. The clause {الله أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِهِنَّ} serves to show that you have no way to what puts the soul at rest and soothes the chest, namely, encompassing the reality of their faith, for that is something Allah has kept for Himself alone. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. And the predominant supposition (ẓann) in his saying «عَلِمْتُموهُنَّ» was called "knowledge" because of the closeness between the two, just as ẓann takes the place of knowledge. This was given earlier in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
And his saying {أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ} means: "in marrying them" (fī an). His saying «إذا آتيْتُمُوهُنَّ» may be a pure adverbial (ẓarf), or a condition whose apodosis (jawāb) is implied, that is: "then there is no blame upon you."
His saying: {وَلاَ تُمْسِكُواْ}: Abū ʿAmr, among others, read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the mīm and shadda on the sīn; the rest of the Seven read it without the shadda, from مَسَّك and أَمْسَك, which have one meaning. One says: أَمْسَكْتُ الحَبْل إمساكاً and مَسَّكْتُه تَمْسكياً. The shadda carries emphasis (mubālagha), though the lightened form is also suited to it. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Laylā, and Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir in a transmission from them, read «تَمَسَّكُوا» with fatḥa throughout and shadda on the sīn. The original is تَتَمسَّكوا with two tāʾs, and one of them was dropped. From al-Ḥasan also: «تَمْسِكوا», the imperfect of the triliteral مَسَكَ. العِصَم is the plural of عِصْمة, and الكوافر is the plural of كافرة, like ضَوارب for ضاربة. It is related of al-Karkhī, the jurist and Muʿtazilite, that he said: الكوافِر includes men and women. Al-Fārisī said: "I said to him, 'The grammarians do not hold this except of women, as a plural of «كافرة».' He said, 'Is it not said: a disbelieving group (ṭāʾifa kāfira), a disbelieving party (firqa kāfira)?' Abū ʿAlī said: I was dumbfounded and said, 'This is divine support.'" I say: he was impressed by his statement only because he was a Muʿtazilite like him. The truth is that «كافِرة» is not permissible as a description of men unless the thing described is mentioned, as in "this is a disbelieving group", or is equivalent to something mentioned. As for saying «كافرة» with respect to an unmentioned group that is not equivalent to something mentioned, but merely as a possibility, and then pluralizing it as a plural of fāʿila, this is not permissible. And al-Fārisī's statement, "they do not hold this except of women," is correct, but that is the predominant case. Sometimes fāʿil, the description of a rational male, is pluralized as fawāʿil, and this is memorized (maḥfūẓ), for example فوارِس and نواكِس.
His saying: {يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The second is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حُكْمُ». The returning pronoun is either latent, that is "it rules", meaning the ruling itself, as an exaggeration, or it is omitted, that is "He rules it". The latter is the apparent one.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {شَيْءٌ مِّنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ}: «مِنْ أزواجِكم» may be attached to «فاتَكم», that is, "from the side of your wives", and by "thing" is meant the dower that the husband was made to pay, because the exegesis has come down that when a Muslim man's wife fled to the disbelievers, Allah the Exalted commanded the believers to give him what he had been made to pay; and the Prophet ﷺ did that with a number of the Companions, who are named in the exegesis. It may also be attached to an omitted element, as a ṣifa (qualifier) of «شيء». Then it is possible that by «شيء» is meant the dowers mentioned earlier, but on this view a muḍāf must be omitted, that is "from the dowers of your wives", so that the thing described and its description agree. It is also possible that by «شيء» is meant women, that is, "something of the women", meaning a kind and sort of them, and that is the apparent sense, and He qualified it with his saying «مِن أزواجِكم».
Al-Zamakhsharī stated this plainly, for he said: "And if something of your wives gets ahead of you and slips away from you, one of them, to the disbelievers" (and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, «أحد»). This is an explicit statement that by «شيء» are meant the women who flee. Then he said: "If you ask: is there any benefit in putting «شيء» in this place? I say: yes, the benefit in it is that nothing of this kind should be left uncompensated, however small and insignificant, as a stiffening of this ruling and a strengthening of it." Had he not stated explicitly that by «شيء» is meant «أحد», as above, his saying "that nothing of this kind should be left, however small and insignificant" would have been apparently meaning that by «شيء» is meant the dower, because it is commonly described as small and insignificant. As for his saying "stiffening and strengthening", there is room for objection, because the Muslims had no part in causing the women to flee to the disbelievers, such that the ruling should be stiffened against them on that account. He made «فات» transitive with «إلى» because it implies the sense of fleeing, going, getting ahead and the like.
His saying: {فَعَاقَبْتُمْ}: a ʿaṭf (conjunction) on «فاتَكم». The majority read «عاقَبْتُم», and there are two possibilities. The first is that it is from العقوبة (punishment). Al-Zajjāj said: "«فعاقبْتُم» means: you struck them in battle with a punishment until you took spoils." The second is that it is from العُقْبة, which is the turn; he likened what was ruled for the Muslims and the disbelievers, namely that these pay the dowers of those's women at one time, and those pay the dowers of these's women at another, to a matter in which they take turns, as turns are taken in riding and the like. Its meaning is: your turn to pay the dower came." End of quotation.
Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, al-Zuhrī, Abū Ḥaywa, ʿIkrima and Ḥumayd read it with shadda on the qāf and no alif. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it, following his principle, as عَقَّبه when he follows behind him, since each of two taking turns follows his companion; likewise «عَقَبْتُم» lightened, of which one says عَقَبه يَعْقُبُه. End. I say: those who read it lightened with fatḥa on the qāf were al-Nakhaʿī, Ibn Wathāb, al-Zuhrī and also al-Aʿraj; and with the light form and kasra on the qāf, Masrūq, al-Zuhrī and also al-Nakhaʿī.
Mujāhid read «أَعْقَبْتُمْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said its meaning is: "you entered into the turn."
As for al-Zajjāj, he explained the remaining readings as: "the outcome (ʿuqbā) was yours", that is, the victory was yours until you took spoils. The apparent sense is as al-Zamakhsharī said, from المعاقبة in the sense of المناوَبة (taking turns). One says: عاقَبَ الرجلُ صاحبَه في كذا, that is, the act of each of the two came after the act of the other; and one also says أَعْقَبَ. And this verse was recited:
4255 - وحارَدَتِ النُّكْدُ الجِلادُ ولم يكُنْ ... لعُقْبَةِ قِدْرِ المُسْتعيرينَ مُعقِبُ
(The stingy, hard-skinned she-camels ran dry, and there was no one to give a turn to the borrowers' pot.)

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {يُبَايِعْنَكَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «شيئاً» is a maṣdar, that is, "anything of associating [others with Allah]". ʿAlī, al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan read «يُقَتِّلْن» with shadda. And «يَفْتَرِيْنَه» is a ṣifa (qualifier) of «بُهتان», or a ḥāl from the agent of «يَأْتين».

semin-durr:13-13.t:
And his saying: {غَضِبَ الله}: a ṣifa (qualifier) of «قَوْماً», and likewise «قد يَئِسُوا».
His saying: {مِنَ الآخرة}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), that is: they have no certainty at all of the Hereafter. And {مِنْ أَصْحَابِ القبور}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it too is for the beginning of the extent, like the first, and the meaning is that they have no certainty at all of the resurrection of the dead, so their despair of the Hereafter is like their despair of their dead, because of their belief that they will not be raised. The second is that it is for specifying the kind (bayān al-jins), meaning that the disbelievers are the people of the graves. The meaning is: these have despaired of the Hereafter as the disbelievers, who are the people of the graves, despaired of the good of the Hereafter; so the second object of "despair" is omitted. Ibn Abī l-Zinād read «الكافرُ» in the singular. And Allah knows best.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ}: these are the two objects of "taking". Since «العدوّ» is on the pattern of maṣdars, it applies to one and to more. He annexed "enemy" to Himself the Exalted to make their crime graver.
His saying: {تُلْقُونَ}: four views. First: it is an explication of their befriending them. Second: it is a resumptive report of that, so the clause on these two views has no position in i'rab. Third: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَتَّخِذوا», i.e., do not take them as allies while extending affection. Fourth: it is an adjective of «أولياءَ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: when you make it an adjective of «أولياء», it runs on other than the one it belongs to, so where is the overt pronoun, which is your saying 'tulqūna ilayhim antum bi-l-mawadda'? I say: they made that a condition in nouns, not in verbs; if it were said 'awliyāʾa mulqīna ilayhim bi-l-mawadda' as an adjective, the overt pronoun would be necessary." I say: this question was treated fully before, and there is a statement of Makkī and others on it. But the Shaykh objected to its being an adjective or a ḥāl, in that they were forbidden to take them as allies absolutely in His saying: {لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ اليهود والنصارى أَوْلِيَآءَ} [al-Māʾida: 51], and restricting it by ḥāl or adjective suggests that taking them as allies is permitted if the ḥāl or adjective is absent. What he said does not follow, because it is known from the rules of the Law, so they have no implication (mafhūm) at all. Al-Farrāʾ said: "«تُلْقون» belongs to the ṣila of «أولياء»", and this accords with their principles, that an indefinite is given a ṣila like other relative nouns.
His saying: {بالمودة}: three views on the bāʾ. One: the bāʾ is redundant in the direct object, as in His saying: {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195]. The second: it is not redundant and the object is omitted, the bāʾ meaning cause, as though it were said: you convey to them the secrets of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his news because of the affection between you. The third: it is attached to the maṣdar indicated by «تُلْقُون», i.e., "their conveying is by affection"; al-Ḥawfī transmitted it from the Basrans and made the view of the bāʾ's redundancy the view of the Kufans. But this which he transmitted from the Basrans does not accord with their principles, since it requires omitting the maṣdar and keeping what it governs, which they do not permit. Also, it involves omitting an entire clause, for «إلقاءَهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «بالمودة» is attached to it, and the khabar is also omitted. This is excessive.
His saying: {وَقَدْ كَفَرُواْ}: several views: resumptive; a ḥāl from the agent of «تتَّخذوا»; a ḥāl from the agent of «تُلْقُون», i.e., do not befriend them or love them, this being their condition. The majority [read] «بما» with bāʾ; al-Jaḥdarī, and ʿĀṣim in one transmission, [read] «لِما» with lām, i.e., because of what came to you; on this the thing disbelieved in is not mentioned, its implied form being: they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger.
His saying: {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول}: it may be resumptive, and it may be an explication of their disbelief, in which case it has no position on these two, and it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «كفروا».
His saying: {وَإِيَّاكُمْ}: conjoined to «الرسول». It was put before them to honour him.
Those who permit separating the pronoun while attachment is possible cite it as evidence, since it could have been said «يُخْرجونكم والرسولَ», so "yukhrijūna iyyākum wa-l-rasūla" would be permitted outside the Quran; it is weak, because the case of putting the Messenger first indicates his nobility. We do not concede that attachment is possible. Your attention has been drawn to this verse at His saying the Exalted {وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ} in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, so consider it.
His saying: {أَن تُؤْمِنُواْ}: an object of purpose; its governor is «يُخْرِجون», i.e., they expel you for your faith or from hating your faith.
His saying: {إِن كُنتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ}: its apodosis is omitted according to the majority because «لا تتَّخذوا» precedes, and it is the preceding one, «لا تتخذوا», according to the Kufans and those who follow them. Its explanation has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{إِنْ كُنتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ} is attached to «لا تَتَّخذوا». He means: do not befriend my enemies if you are my friends. The grammarians' saying in the like of it is: it is a condition whose apodosis is omitted because what precedes indicates it." End of quotation. He means that it is attached to it in meaning; as for i'rab, it is as the majority of grammarians said.
His saying: «جِهَاداً وابتغآء»: they may both be accusative as objects of purpose, i.e., "you went out for these two", or as maṣdars of an implied verb, i.e., "you strive and you seek", or as being in the position of ḥāl.
His saying: {تُسِرُّونَ}: it may be resumptive; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only that; it may be a second ḥāl from what «تُلْقُون» was accusative from as a ḥāl; and it may be a badal from «تُلْقُون», as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said. It resembles being a badal of inclusion, because conveying affection may be secret or open, so this was substituted from it to clarify by which kind the conveying occurred; and it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e., "you conceal", as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, and it does not leave the meaning of resumption. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is an emphasis of «تُلْقُون» by repeating its meaning." There is something to consider in it, because conveying is more general than being secret or open.
And His saying: {بالمودة}: what is said about the bāʾ here is like what is said about it after «تُلْقُون».
His saying: {وَأَنَاْ أَعْلَمُ}: this clause is a ḥāl from the agent of «تُسِرُّون», i.e., what gain is there for you in your concealing, when you know that concealing and announcing are alike in My knowledge? «أعلمُ» may be the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), which is the apparent view, and it may be an imperfect verb. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is made transitive by the bāʾ because you say 'ʿalimtu bi-kadhā'."
His saying: {وَمَن يَفْعَلْهُ}: two views on the pronoun. The more apparent is that it returns to concealing, because it is the nearest mentioned. The second: it returns to the taking [of allies]; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it.
His saying: {سَوَآءَ السبيل}: it may be accusative as an adverbial if we say «ضَلَّ» is intransitive, and it may be a direct object if we say it is transitive.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {وَوَدُّواْ لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ}: there are two views on «وَدُّوا». One: it is conjoined to the apodosis of the condition, which is «يكونوا» and «يَبْسُطوا»; al-Zamakhsharī said so. Then he built on it a question and answer, saying: "If you say: how did He bring the apodosis of the condition in the imperfect like it, then say «وَدُّوا» in the past form? I say: the past, although it runs in the chapter of conditions the same course as the imperfect as to i'rab knowledge, has a subtle point in it, as though it were said: 'and they wished, before everything else, your disbelief and your apostasy', meaning that they want to inflict on you the harms of this world and the next together." The second: it is conjoined to the sentence of condition and result, so the Exalted would have given two reports: what the conditional sentence contains, and their wish for the believers' disbelief. The Shaykh made this the preferred view and thereby dropped al-Zamakhsharī's question and answer, saying: "Al-Zamakhsharī understood from «وَوَدُّوا» that it is conjoined to the apodosis of the condition. What appears is that it is not conjoined to it, because their wishing for their disbelief is not consequent on getting the upper hand over them and being given power over them; rather they wish for their disbelief in every case, whether they overcome them or do not overcome them." End of quotation.
I say: the apparent view is that it is conjoined to the apodosis. His saying that they wish for that absolutely is conceded, but their wishing for it at the time of victory and power is nearer and they covet it more then.
And His saying: {لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ}: it may be [lau] "for what will occur because of the occurrence of [something else]", and it may be the maṣdar particle according to those who hold that; both have been explained in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ القيامة}: two views are possible. One: it is attached to what precedes, i.e., "it will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection", so one pauses there and begins «يَفْصِلُ بينكم». The second: it is attached to what follows, i.e., "He will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection", so one pauses at «أولادكم» and begins «يوم القيامة».
The readers differ on «يَفْصِلُ» «بينكم» in four ranks. First: for Ibn ʿĀmir, with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the fāʾ, and doubled ṣād. Second: likewise, but with kasra on the ṣād, for the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī]. Third: for ʿĀṣim, with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the fāʾ and lightened ṣād with kasra. Fourth: with ḍamma on the yāʾ, sukūn on the fāʾ and lightened ṣād with fatḥa, for the rest, who are Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr; this among the Seven. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Ḥaywa read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, sukūn on the fāʾ and lightened ṣād with kasra, from afṣala. Abū Ḥaywa also [read] «نُفْصِلُ» with ḍamma on the nūn, from afṣala. Al-Nakhaʿī and Ṭalḥa [read] «نُفَصِّلُ» with ḍamma on the nūn, fatḥa on the fāʾ and doubled ṣād with kasra. He (Ṭalḥa) also read, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī, «نَفْصِلُ» with fatḥa on the nūn, sukūn on the fāʾ and lightened ṣād with kasra. These are four, making eight readings.
Whoever made it passive, the deputy agent is either the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e., "the judgment is judged", or the adverbial, which was built on fatḥa because of its annexation to something not fully inflected, as in {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] on one view; or the adverbial, remaining in its accusative, as you say "juliesa ʿindaka" (it was sat by you).

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِمَا جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ الْحَقِّ يُخْرِجُونَ الرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهَادًا فِي سَبِيلِي وَابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِي تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِمَا أَخْفَيْتُمْ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُمْ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْهُ مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ (١))
His saying (تُلْقُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «تَتَّخِذُوا», and it may be resumptive. The bāʾ in «بِالْمَوَدَّةِ» is redundant (zāʾida). And (يُخْرِجُونَ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «كَفَرُوا», or resumptive.
And (إِيَّاكُمْ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرَّسُول. And (أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), governed by «يُخْرِجُونَ».
And (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ): its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by لَا تَتَّخِذُوا.
And (جِهَادًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, or governed by an omitted verb indicated by the context, i.e. "you strove a striving (جَاهَدْتُمْ جِهَادًا)". And (تُسِرُّونَ) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of تُلْقُونَ, by repeating its meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الْكَوَافِرِ وَاسْأَلُوا مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ. . . (١٠))
And (تُمْسِكُوا) has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.
(يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا جَاءَكَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ يُبَايِعْنَكَ عَلَى أَنْ لَا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَسْرِقْنَ وَلَا يَزْنِينَ وَلَا يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ وَلَا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتَانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ وَلَا يَعْصِينَكَ فِي مَعْرُوفٍ فَبَايِعْهُنَّ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُنَّ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٢))
And (يُبَايِعْنَكَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (يَفْتَرِينَهُ) is a naʿt (adjective) of بُهْتَانٍ, or a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in «يَأْتِينَ».
«[Translator's note: this entry, keyed to verse 10, also contains the comment on verse 12.]»

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ كَمَا يَئِسَ الْكُفَّارُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْقُبُورِ (١٣))
His saying (مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْقُبُورِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَئِسَ, i.e. "they despaired of the resurrection of the inhabitants of the graves"; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being among the inhabitants of the graves".

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ أَرْحَامُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ. . . (٣))
His saying (يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ): an adverb (ẓarf) for «يَفْصِلُ», or for His saying «لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ».
In «يَفْصِلُ» there are several readings whose i'rab is evident; except that whoever reads it with the agent unnamed (passive) makes «بَيْنَكُمْ» stand in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil), as we mentioned on His saying (لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ إِذْ قَالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إِنَّا بُرَآءُ مِنْكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ وَبَدَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَالْبَغْضَاءُ أَبَدًا حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ إِلَّا قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَمَا أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ رَبَّنَا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ (٤))
His saying (فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ): there are several views on it.
The first: it is another naʿt (adjective) of أُسْوَةٌ.
The second: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَسَنَةٌ», as an adverbial is attached to what governs it. The third: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «حَسَنَةٌ». The fourth: it is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and «لَكُمْ» is for clarification (tabyīn). It cannot be attached to أُسْوَةٌ, because that has [already] been described.
And (إِذْ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for the khabar of كَانَ; it may also itself be the khabar of كَانَ.
And (بُرَآءُ) is the plural of بَرِيءٍ, like ظَرِيفٍ and ظُرَفَاءُ. And بُرَاءُ with a single hamza is like رُخَالٍ; it is said: the [other] hamza has been omitted; it is also said: it is a plural in its own right. And بِرَاءٌ with kasra is like ظِرَافٍ. And with fatḥa [بَرَاءٌ] it is a noun of the maṣdar, like سَلَامٍ, and the implied form is "we are people of disavowal (ذَوُو بَرَاءٍ)".
His saying (إِلَّا قَوْلَ): it is an exception from a different genus (min ghayr al-jins), and the meaning is: "do not follow his example in asking forgiveness for the disbelievers".

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِيهِمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِمَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ. . . (٦))
His saying (لِمَنْ كَانَ): this has been mentioned in al-Aḥzāb.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَنْهَاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ. . . (٨))
His saying (أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ): it is in the position of the genitive [as a badal (substitute)] from الَّذِينَ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), i.e. "from being good to those who…"; and likewise (أَنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ).

zajjaj:2-2.t: Then Allah the Exalted informed them that seeking closeness to them by passing on the reports of the Prophet ﷺ would not benefit them, and He said: ﴿إنْ يَثْقَفُوكم يَكُونُوا لَكم أعْداءً﴾. The meaning of ”يَثْقَفُوكُمْ“ is: they meet you (find you). ﴿وَيَبْسُطُوا إلَيْكم أيْدِيَهم وألْسِنَتَهم بِالسُّوءِ﴾.

zajjaj:3-3.t: Then He informed them that their kin and their children will not benefit them at all on the Day of Resurrection, and He said: ﴿لَنْ تَنْفَعَكم أرْحامُكم ولا أوْلادُكم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾. ”يَفْصِلُ“ has been read in four ways: ”يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“, in the sense of "Allah will judge between you"; ”يُفْصَلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), the meaning referring back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; ”يُفَصَّلَ بَيْنَكُمْ“, with a doubled ṣād carrying a fatḥa and a ḍamma on the yāʾ, again as a verb whose agent is not named; and it was read ”يُفَصِّلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“. It is also permissible to say ”نُفَصِّلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“ and ”نَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“, with nūn. So these are six ways.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قَدْ كانَتْ لَكم أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ﴾ — it is also permissible to say ”أُسْوَةٌ“ with a ḍamma on the hamza [Translator's note: the word as printed already carries a ḍamma; the intended contrast is presumably with the kasra form إسْوة] — ﴿فِي إبْراهِيمَ والَّذِينَ مَعَهُ إذْ قالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إنّا بُرَآءُ مِنكم ومِمّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the companions of Ibrāhīm — Allah's blessings be upon him — disowned their people and showed them enmity, and He commanded the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ to take them, and their words, as an example.

His saying: ﴿إلا قَوْلَ إبْراهِيمَ لأبِيهِ لأسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ﴾ — that was only because of a promise he had made him; then when it became clear to him that he persisted in disbelief, he disowned him. As for what is permissible in ”بُرَءاءُ مِنكُمْ“, there are four ways. The best of them is ”بُرَءاءُ“ on the pattern ”فُعَلاءُ“, like ”ظَرِيفٌ“ / ”ظُرَفاءُ“ and ”شَرِيكٌ“ / ”شُرَكاءُ“; likewise ”بَرِيءٌ“ / ”بُرَءاءُ“. It is also permissible to say ”بُراءٌ مِنكُمْ“ and ”بَراءٌ مِنكُمْ“ [Translator's note: the third form, discussed next, is printed here as بَراء, while the explanation that follows is of بِراء with kasra], both with madd (a long vowel). Whoever says ”بِراءٌ“ with madd treats it like ”ظَرِيفٌ“ / ”ظِرافٌ“; and whoever says ”بُراءٌ“ with ḍamma has substituted the ḍamma for the kasra, just as they said ”رُخْلَةٌ“ / ”رِخالٌ“, and some of them said ”رُخالٌ“ with a ḍamma on the rāʾ; and they said ”شاةٌ رُبًّى“ (a recently-delivered ewe), with ”غَنَمٌ رُبابٌ“ and ”رِبابٌ“, with ḍamma and kasra on the rāʾ — that is, the one that has recently given birth, i.e. recently delivered. It is also permissible to say ”بَراءٌ مِنكُمْ“ with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, because the Arabs say ”أنا البَراءُ مِنكَ“ (I am quit of you), and two or three people say ”نَحْنُ البَراءُ مِنكَ“, and likewise a woman says ”أنا البَراءُ مِنكَ“. But do not recite any of these ways except what has been recited by someone from whom the reading is transmitted.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — its meaning is: do not give them victory over us, so that they think they are in the right and are thereby led astray (yuftatanū).

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿عَسى اللَّهُ أنْ يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ عادَيْتُمْ مِنهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ — ”عَسى“ from Allah is binding (certain). It has come in the exegesis that by this He means that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umm Ḥabība, daughter of Abū Sufyān, and that this is the affection. It is also said that He means by it those of them who embraced Islam, so that there would be affection between you and them.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿لا يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقاتِلُوكم في الدِّينِ ولَمْ يُخْرِجُوكم مِن دِيارِكم أنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ﴾ — ”أنْ“ is in the position of the genitive, a badal (substitute) for ”اَلَّذِينَ“. The meaning is: "He does not forbid you from being kind to those who did not fight you on account of religion." This indicates that the meaning is: "Allah does not forbid you from being kind to those between whom and you there is a covenant," and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَتُقْسِطُوا إلَيْهِمْ﴾, i.e. and that you act justly in what is between you and them, by fulfilling the covenant. One says ”أقْسَطَ الرَّجُلُ، فَهو مُقْسِطٌ“ when he acts justly, and ”قَسَطَ، فَهو قاسِطٌ“ when he acts unjustly. It is also said that He means by it women and children.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّما يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ قاتَلُوكم في الدِّينِ وأخْرَجُوكم مِن دِيارِكم وظاهَرُوا عَلى إخْراجِكم أنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾ — ”ظاهَرُوا عَلى إخْراجِكُمْ“ means: they helped one another in expelling you. ﴿أنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾: ”أنْ“ is also in the position of the genitive, as a badal (substitute). The meaning is: "Allah only forbids you from taking as allies these who fought you on account of religion," because writing to them by disclosing what the Prophet ﷺ had kept secret is alliance (muwālāt).

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا جاءَكُمُ المُؤْمِناتُ مُهاجِراتٍ﴾ — the position of ”مُهاجِراتٍ“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). They were called ”اَلْمُؤْمِناتُ“ (the believing women) even though they were not known for faith and before they reached the Prophet ﷺ; they were only named so because faith was presumed of them. ﴿فامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾ means: test them. This was revealed because of the covenant of al-Ḥudaybiya which was between the Prophet ﷺ and those in Makka who made a covenant with him, of Khuzāʿa and others. He ﷺ had made a covenant with them that whoever came to him from them he would return to them, and whoever went over to them from him they would not return to him. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that whoever of the believing women came, of those who wished to enter Islam, were not to be returned to the disbelievers; that is His saying: ﴿فامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِإيمانِهِنَّ﴾. So He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that outward profession of faith comes within the scope of Islam, while Allah knows what is in the hearts. The test, when an emigrant woman came, was that she be made to swear by Allah that it was not resentment against her husband that brought her, and that she came only out of love for Allah and His Messenger and out of desire for Islam; this was the test. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَلا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إلى الكُفّارِ﴾ means: do not send them back. One says ”رَجَعَ فُلانٌ“ (so-and-so returned) and ”رَجَعْتُهُ“ (I returned him).

His saying: ﴿لا هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَهم ولا هم يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ﴾ means: the believing women are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for the believing women. ﴿وَآتُوهم ما أنْفَقُوا﴾ — the husband used to be given the dowry of his wife who had believed, and the dowry used to be taken from them for whichever of the believers' wives went over to them, of those who joined her husband when she inclined to disbelief and persisted in it. ﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ means: there is no sin upon you ﴿أنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾, i.e. in marrying them, ﴿إذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾; this is evidence that marriage must include a dowry. ﴿وَلا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الكَوافِرِ﴾ means: when they disbelieve, the tie (ʿiṣma) between the polytheist woman and the believer has ceased, i.e. the knot of the rope of marriage has been severed. The root meaning of ”اَلْعِصْمَةُ“ is a rope, and whatever holds something has "held fast" (ʿaṣama) it. It was read ”وَلا تُمْسِكُوا“ and ”وَلا تَمَسَّكُوا“, the original being ”تَتَمَسَّكُوا“, from your saying ”تَمَسَّكْتُ بِالشَّيْءِ“ (I held on to the thing), when you do not let it go from your hand or your will; one of the two tāʾs was elided. It was read ”تُمَسَّكُوا“ with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and doubling, from your saying ”مَسَّكَ، يُمَسِّكُ“ [Translator's note: the vowelling تُمَسَّكُوا as printed has a fatḥa on the sīn; the form derived from مَسَّكَ يُمَسِّكُ would be تُمَسِّكُوا]; and it was read ”تُمْسِكُوا“ with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and the sīn undoubled, in the sense of ”أمْسَكَ، يُمْسِكُ“.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنْ فاتَكم شَيْءٌ مِن أزْواجِكم إلى الكُفّارِ فَعاقَبْتُمْ﴾ — on the pattern ”فاعَلْتُمْ“. It was also read ”فَعَقَبْتُمْ“, without alif and with an undoubled qāf. It has come in the exegesis: "and you took spoils." Its interpretation in the language is: "the outcome (al-ʿuqbā) was yours," i.e. "the outcome and the victory were yours, so that you took spoils." ”عَقِبْتُمْ“ [Translator's note: so printed; the context, which speaks next of the undoubled form and then says the doubled form is more emphatic, suggests the doubled form عَقَّبْتُم was intended] is the best of them in the language, and ”فَعَقَبْتُمْ“ without doubling is also good in the language, i.e. "the outcome of victory became yours," except that with doubling it is more emphatic. The meaning of ﴿فَعاقَبْتُمْ﴾ is: you struck them in battle with a punishment until you took spoils; i.e. if a woman of yours went off to those between whom and you there is no covenant, ﴿فَآتُوا الَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتْ أزْواجُهم مِثْلَ ما أنْفَقُوا﴾, i.e. the like of what they spent on their dowries. Likewise if she went off to those between whom and you there is a covenant and they broke faith in paying the dowry: the one whose wife had gone used to be given the dowry from the spoils, so that nothing of his right was diminished; he was given his right in full after the women's dowries were taken out. It is for this reason that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may Allah have mercy on him — paid, according to what they have related, the dowry of Umm Ayman.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا جاءَكَ المُؤْمِناتُ يُبايِعْنَكَ عَلى أنْ لا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا ولا يَسْرِقْنَ ولا يَزْنِينَ ولا يَقْتُلْنَ أوْلادَهُنَّ ولا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِنَّ وأرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾ means: they will not bring a child which they attribute to the husband, for that is a slander and a fabrication. ﴿وَلا يَعْصِينَكَ في مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ — it is said: they will not disobey you in a matter concerning wailing (over the dead); and it is said: in tearing clothes, scratching faces and conversing with men. The sum of it is that the meaning is: "they will not disobey you in anything you command them that is right."

It is related «that the Prophet ﷺ sat on al-Ṣafā, and ʿUmar — may Allah have mercy on him — sat below him, and they would pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ on what the verse contains, and wipe their hands on the hand of ʿUmar. And it is said: "they used to wipe with their hands from behind a garment."»

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الآخِرَةِ﴾ — He means by it the Jews. ﴿كَما يَئِسَ الكُفّارُ مِن أصْحابِ القُبُورِ﴾ means: just as the disbelievers who do not believe with certainty in the resurrection have despaired of their dead being raised, so the Jews and those who made a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ have despaired of having any share in the Hereafter. And it is said: ﴿قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الآخِرَةِ كَما يَئِسَ الكُفّارُ مِن أصْحابِ القُبُورِ﴾ means: of those who are in the graves; they know that they have no share in the Hereafter. [Translator's note: i.e. on this view the despairing disbelievers are themselves the people of the graves.]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Mumtaḥana
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وعَدُوَّكم أوْلِياءَ تُلْقُونَ إلَيْهِمْ بِالمَوَدَّةِ﴾ — it has been said that the meaning is: "تُلْقُونَ إلَيْهِمُ المَوَدَّةَ" (you offer them affection) [Translator's note: i.e. with the bāʾ redundant]. But the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "they convey to them the news of the Prophet, upon him be peace, and his secret, by reason of the affection that is between you and them". The evidence for this view is ﴿تُسِرُّونَ إلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Mumtaḥana: 1]: (you secretly pass on to them) what the Prophet, upon him be peace, keeps hidden, out of affection. It is transmitted «that it was revealed concerning Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa. He had written to the people of Mecca, professing sincere counsel to them, and wrote to them: "The Messenger of Allah intends to campaign against you, so take your precautions." Allah informed His Prophet of that. He had written them a letter and sent it with a woman who, it is said, was a client (mawlāt) of the Banū Hāshim. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAlī and al-Zubayr after her. They caught up with her and asked her about the letter, but she denied it. They searched what she had with her and found nothing. Then ʿAlī, may Allah's good pleasure be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not told us a lie", and ʿAlī swore to her that she would bring out the letter or he would strike her with the sword. She said to them: "Turn your faces away", and brought out the letter from one of the plaits of her hair. He brought the letter to the Prophet, upon him be peace, who showed it to Ḥāṭib; he admitted it and said: "I have family and property in Mecca, so I wanted to gain favour with them; and Allah will not turn His might away from them." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾ (the verse), to the end of the account.»
As for His saying: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهادًا في سَبِيلِي وابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِي﴾ — this is a condition (sharṭ) whose answer (jawāb al-sharṭ, apodosis) has come before it; the meaning is: "if you have gone out striving in My way and seeking My good pleasure, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies". "جِهادًا" and "اِبْتِغاءَ" are both accusative (manṣūb) because they are mafʿūl lahu (objects of purpose); the meaning is: "if you have gone out for striving and seeking My good pleasure, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies."
